newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields close lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields close lower on consolidation.

text.p: Consolidation in reaction to recent steep rises in three-year benchmark corporate yields pushed the yields to a lower close, dealers said on Wednesday.
"Securities houses tried to take profits in the corporate bonds following recent rises," said a Sunkyong Securities dealer. "But the consolidation seemed to be temporary."
A Ssangyong Securities dealer attributed today's fall mainly to a lack of selling amid a small number of new corporate bond issues.
About 26.5 billion won worth of new corporates were issued on Wednesday against a daily average of 100 billion.
"I believe money demand ahead of Chusok seemed to be almost finished. So the corporate yield will be in consolidation to the 12.20 level," said the Ssangyong Securities dealer.
He said there would be no liquidity squeeze by the monetary authority.
But the Sunkyong Securities dealer said the three-year yield would soon hit a new year high of 12.70, given the pessimistic economic outlook and a tight corporate money situation.
Dealers said the overnight call rate would rise by a 0.5 percentage point per day over the next three days and then start falling. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
